header.name: mneme
header.tagline: Every recall re-derives, and every stale memory says so.

flows.kicker: one question, answered from the record
flows.title: How a recall becomes a ranking someone else can re-derive
flows.footnote: The ranking is re-derived from the rows, never read back from the receipt.
flows.alt: Eight stages of a verifiable recall: turn, atom, scenario, persona, query, score, fuse, receipt. Raw dialogue is stored verbatim as a turn and never summarized away. An atom is one fact bound to the turn it came from, a scenario groups related atoms, and a persona cites its atoms instead of prose. A query records its own scope. Keyword scoring is pure Python BM25 and always available; reciprocal rank fusion folds in a vector channel when an embedder is supplied. The receipt carries the ranked hits, both score channels, the scorer-definition hash, and the fusion rule. Verification re-runs the same scorer over the same rows and compares. Two outcomes: reproduced, and did not reproduce.

stages.title: Turn
stages.note: Raw dialogue, stored whole and never summarized.

stages.title: Atom
stages.note: One fact, bound to the turn it was taken from.

stages.title: Scenario
stages.note: Related atoms, grouped into one scene.

stages.title: Persona
stages.note: A profile that cites atoms, not prose.

stages.title: Query
stages.note: One question, with its scope recorded.

stages.title: Score
stages.note: BM25 in pure Python, with no dependency.

stages.title: Fuse
stages.note: Rank fusion folds in the vector channel.

stages.title: Receipt
stages.note: The hits, both scores, and the fusion rule.

returns.label: VERIFY RE-RUNS THE SCORER OVER THE SAME ROWS

outcomes.label: REPRODUCED
outcomes.note: the same rows re-derive the same ranking

outcomes.label: DID NOT REPRODUCE
outcomes.note: a tampered ranking, or a store that moved

flows.kicker: one memory, checked against its source
flows.title: How a stored fact reports for itself that it has gone stale
flows.footnote: A source that is gone is unverifiable, never a vacuous match.
flows.alt: Eight stages of a freshness check: memory, own hash, sources, re-hash, snapshot, compare, fold, verdict. The memory row must first reproduce its own content hash, which catches a direct edit of its text, sources, or criterion. Each cited source is then re-hashed from its actual fields rather than trusted from a stored hash, so a direct database edit cannot preserve a stale value and pass. The current bytes are compared against the hash recorded at extraction time. The fold takes any change first, then any absence, and only then a match. Three outcomes: match, drift, and unverifiable.

stages.title: Memory
stages.note: One fact, and the criterion it was kept under.

stages.title: Own hash
stages.note: The row must reproduce its own hash first.

stages.title: Sources
stages.note: Every id it cites: a turn, or a memory.

stages.title: Re-hash
stages.note: The source's real fields, hashed again now.

stages.title: Snapshot
stages.note: The hash taken when the fact was extracted.

stages.title: Fold
stages.note: Any change first, then any absence.

stages.title: Verdict
stages.note: Per memory, and across the whole store.

returns.label: THE COMPARE REPEATS FOR EVERY SOURCE CITED

outcomes.label: MATCH
outcomes.note: every source is present and unchanged

outcomes.label: DRIFT
outcomes.note: a source changed under the memory

outcomes.label: UNVERIFIABLE
outcomes.note: a source is gone, or none was cited
